data.long_meaning: Celestina is a Latin name derived from the word celestis, meaning 'heavenly' or 'celestial'. In Christianity, this name is often associated with the Virgin Mary, as she is the one who brought God's grace to earth. Celestina is also the name of several saints, including St. Celestina of Rome, who was a martyr in the 4th century.

data.etymology: Celestina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Heavenly, Celestial.”

in_greek.name: Κελεστίνα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κελεστίνα προέρχεται από τη λατινική και σημαίνει ουράνιος, αποτελείται από τις λέξεις Coelestis, που σημαίνει ουράνιος, και το θηλυκό суφίξ İnă, που είναι θηλυκή εκδοχή, και σε ευρύτερη έννοια αναφέρεται σε άγγελο ή αγγελιοφόρο του Θεού

in_latin.name: Coelestina

in_english.name: Celestina
in_english.long_meaning: The name Celestina is derived from Latin and means heavenly, it is composed of the words Coelestis, meaning heavenly, and the suffix Ina, which is a feminine termination, and in a broader sense it refers to an angel or messenger of God

data.cultural_impact: The name Celestina has a rich and enduring cultural significance, particularly in the Western world. It is a name that evokes the heavenly realm and the mystical qualities of the divine. In literature, Celestina is the title of a novel by Fernando de Rojas, published in 1514, which is considered a classic example of the picaresque novel. The character Celestina in the novel is an old, wise, and powerful woman who uses her knowledge of human nature to manipulate those around her. The name has also been used in music, with songs such as "Celestina" by Mariza, which explores the theme of love and the longing for the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Celestina carries a deep spiritual significance. It reminds us of the heavenly realm and the divine beings who inhabit it. The name is a reminder of the power and grace of God, and the aspiration to live a life that is pleasing to Him. The name Celestina also evokes the Blessed Virgin Mary, who is the ultimate embodiment of the celestial realm. By calling someone by this name, we are acknowledging their divine potential and expressing our hopes and prayers for their spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Celestina: Heavenly, celestial dweller, connected deeply to the divine realm, embodying purity and grace from the heavens.

historical_references.reference: Celestina of Rome, a renowned Christian virgin and martyr, is believed to have lived during the late 3rd or early 4th century. She is said to have been a member of a noble Roman family and was subjected to various forms of torture and torment before being executed. Her feast day is celebrated on November 25th.

Celestina of Gorizia, also known as the 'Good of Gorizia', was a Benedictine abbess in the 13th century. She is known for her extraordinary charitable works and her ability to perform miracles. Her relics are now housed in the Basilica of Saint Feliciano in Gorizia, Italy.
